# relay_api_key (Resource)

An organization or workspace API key. A key created with an API key is its child: it cannot outlive it or reach past its allowed addresses, and revoking the parent revokes it. The secret is returned once, at creation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "relay_api_key" "ci" {
  name          = "ci"
  role          = "admin"
  allowed_cidrs = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
  expires_in    = "2160h"
}

resource "relay_api_key" "deployer" {
  name         = "deployer"
  workspace_id = relay_workspace.prod.id
  role         = "viewer"
}

output "ci_key" {
  value     = relay_api_key.ci.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, up to 100 characters. Names need not be unique.
- `role` (String) Role slug granted to the key, such as `admin` or `viewer`. It cannot grant a permission the caller lacks, nor an owner-level role. Changes in place.

### Optional

- `allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) IP addresses or CIDR blocks the key may be used from, up to 20. Omit it to allow any address, or the parent key's addresses.
- `expires_in` (String) Lifetime as a duration, such as `720h`, at most `8760h`. Counted from the apply that sets or changes it. Omit it for a key that never expires, or that expires with its parent.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the key is confined to. Omit it for an organization key. Changing it replaces the key.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time, RFC 3339.
- `effective_allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) Addresses the platform enforces: `allowed_cidrs` normalized to CIDR blocks, or the parent key's when `allowed_cidrs` is empty.
- `expires_at` (String) Expiry, RFC 3339. Null when the key never expires.
- `id` (String) API key ID.
- `parent_key_id` (String) ID of the API key that created this one, empty when a user did.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The `rly_key_…` secret, stored in state. Not recoverable from the API, so it is null after an import.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import relay_api_key.ci <key_id>
terraform import relay_api_key.deployer <workspace_id>/<key_id>
```
